subject: Transportation Systems
title: Transit and City Shape
description: One-minute skill: Transit and City Shape.

hook.text: The type of transit a city builds determines its shape for generations.

buildup.text: Rail cities grow in dense corridors along train lines. Car cities spread outward in every direction.

discovery.text: Tokyo, Paris, and Hong Kong are rail cities—dense, walkable, with transit at their core.

twist.text: Houston, Phoenix, and Dubai were built around highways. Retrofitting transit into car cities is brutal.

climax.text: The transit decision made 80 years ago still controls how—and whether—a city works today.

punchline.text: Build rails, get density. Build highways, get sprawl.

quiz.question: How does transit type affect city shape?
options: It doesn't affect it at all
Rail creates dense corridors; highways create sprawl
All transit produces the same shape
